description:
From the fz-kdt.198 research (2026-09-03, 8de517a28). The @spec gate is
argument-side only: apply_function_contract checks the arguments against
the clause domains (spec_violation at a user callsite) and REFINES the
observed return by the declared one (refine_observed_return), but nothing
ever asks whether the body's return evidence is INSIDE the declared return.
Six lines, no diagnostic, on three doors:
    defmodule M do
      @spec pick(binary) :: integer
      fn pick(b), do: b
    end
    fn main(), do: dbg(M.pick(<<104, 105>>))   # prints "hi"
Same for `@spec make() :: integer` returning a binary, and `@spec make() ::
utf8` returning a bare binary. This is why fz-kdt.198's lattice fix has 0
corpus movers: the runtime library's only brand traffic (Utf8.from_bytes! ::
utf8, from_bytes :: {:ok, utf8}) sits at RETURN positions that nothing gates.
SEQUENCE: once the return side is checked, `any ⊄ utf8` bites on Utf8 (its
values are minted by an extern returning any), so this needs the owner's
decision on a minting form for branded values (recorded on fz-kdt.198)
FIRST, then lands as: the settled return of an activation with a declared
contract must be a subtype of the instantiated declared return, else a
diagnostic at the definition (not the callsite), with the same library/
user gating as fz-kdt.33. CONCORDANCE: fz-kdt.2 (protocol-domain @spec
obligations never validated -- the protocol half of the same gap), fz-
kdt.33 (where enforcement is gated), fz-kdt.37 (declared parameters that
silently degrade to any), fz-kdt.198 (the brand model this makes bite),
fz-kdt.190 (how a declared return refines the join today).

comments.text: fz-kdt.203 (2026-09-03): the brand slot is per-descriptor, so `utf8 | nil` loses the brand under fz-kdt.198. Checking a @spec RETURN that names a brand (the only interesting return check for brands) cannot be trusted until 203 puts the slot on each DNF clause. The non-brand half of 201 (a declared return whose kind the body does not meet) does not wait on 203.

fz-kdt.198 landed (4c3fa4c63): the lattice now says `utf8 <: binary`, so a checked return would be meaningful for the single-brand case; the union case still waits on fz-kdt.203. Related finding from the refutation, at base and here: callable DOMAINS are not checked at a @spec ARGUMENT position either -- `(integer) -> int` is accepted where `(binary) -> int` is declared, and so is the reverse (probes s9/s10 in the 198 research archive). That is the argument-side sibling of this ticket's return-side gap; filed as fz-kdt.207.

title: [BUG] A @spec's declared RETURN is never checked against the body: `@spec pick(binary) :: integer; fn pick(b), do: b` is accepted and prints "hi"
